claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The nearest previously published mathematical record, "Sharp radial-population boundary for nonmonotone commuting shares in the finite radiation model", studies the nonmonotone probability of an individual intermediate destination under origin-population variation. Its one-share extremum criterion does not state or imply the variance curve's exact three positive extrema or the sharp two-destination impossibility. Identical underlying radiation probability law is acknowledged; the new claim concerns the variance across three distinct distances and a new factorized polynomial. A counterexample for one component share does not imply even one variance extremum, because second moments and covariances of all shares enter; our exact three-extrema result is not a mathematical corollary of the recorded one-share threshold alone.

value.rationale: Addresses the natural dispersion-versus-distance-shift distinction in finite spatial commuting models. Shows that strict outward first-order stochastic drift coexists with THREE sign changes of variance derivative and proves three destination types are required, so the effect is minimal rather than an arbitrary high-dimensional example. Exact factoring, full positive population range and distinct regimes provide a reproducible structural benchmark for heterogeneity diagnostics; no empirical validation or broad characterization is claimed.
